specification.objective: Make audit ID filters match substrings and replace technical action, entity-type, and result text filters with readable Portuguese dropdowns.

requirements.statement: Actor user ID, entity ID, and project ID filters match any literal substring of the corresponding identifier before pagination, without bypassing company scope.
Action, entity type, and result filters are selectable from Portuguese dropdown labels while sending the existing technical values to the API.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Backend regression tests verify partial actor, entity, and project ID matches, including literal wildcard characters, through the audit list endpoint; CSV export continues to reuse the same filters.
Widget tests verify action, entity-type, and result are Portuguese dropdowns in the audit filter UI, and applying them forwards their technical values alongside partial ID strings.
docs/contracts/audit-filter-search-v1.polis.json is byte-for-byte identical to the locked contract.

invariants.statement: Preserve tenant/company isolation, date and exact action/type/result filtering, sorting, pagination, export behavior, and existing accessibility labels and controls.

forbidden_states.statement: Partial IDs are treated as exact values or SQL wildcard syntax; any query exposes another company's events; or dropdown labels expose only technical codes/lose the API values.

inputs.statement: Audit filter text for actor user ID, entity ID, and project ID, plus selected action, entity type, and result options.

outputs.statement: Paginated audit rows and CSV exports matching ID substrings, with localized Portuguese filter choices for action, entity type, and result.

failure_semantics.statement: The focused audit filter widget test fails with audit_filter_dropdowns_pt_br when the fields are not Portuguese dropdowns or selected API values are incorrect.

argv: audit filters and known event values are presented in pt-BR while requests keep technical IDs
audit filters and known event values are presented in pt-BR while requests keep technical IDs
